sentences.text:
1 2 . The instant petition is filed by a senior citizen, under Section 528 of BNSS, for quashing of FIR bearing number 521/2024 dated 05.08.2024, registered at Police Station Jhotwara, Jaipur City (West), for offences under sections 420, 468, 406, 467, 471  (Downloaded on 26/10/2024 at 11:52:15 PM)
 [2024:RJ-JP:41460] (2 of 5) [CRLMP-5288/2024]
and 120B of I.P.C., along with the consequential proceedings arising therefrom.
3.
The factual narrative is that the instant petition is filed by Shri Amar Singh Chouhan through a Power of Attorney (hereinafter referred to as PoA) holder Shri Dushyant Jadon.

Mr.
Chouhan on account of his ill-health and elderly age, appointed Mr.
Jadon as his PoA holder vide PoA dated 03.01.2023, qua a piece of land (1 bigha land located on Khasra No. 575, village Jhotwara,
Jaipur) that is owned and is under possession of the petitioner.

4. In this backdrop, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that on an erstwhile occasion the complainant's mother i.e. Smt. Geeta Devi lodged an F.I.R.
bearing number 240/2023 dated 11.04.2023 for offences under sections 420, 467, 468, 380 and 120B of I.P.C. against the petitioner and his family members, regarding plot no. 39 to 43,
Scheme Ramnathpuri, Kalwar Road, Jhotwara, Jaipur vis--vis forged documents and forced encroachment of the property wherein, the police authorities have filed a charge sheet against the accused-petitioner for offences under section 420, 406, 467,

2 468, 471, 453, 380 and 120B of I.P.C. (Annexure-2).
5.
Moreover, now the complainant along with their other family members who are land mafias are trying to arrogate the property that per se belongs to the petitioner.

Further, it was submitted that the petitioner along with his family, is in possession of /residing in the said property, from past fifty years, and resultant to the instant dispute a civil suit is already is subjudice before the competent authority/court, for declaration and permanent injunction.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and the Investigating Officer (present in the Court) have stoutly opposed the contentions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner and had raised a preliminary objection qua the locus standi of the petitioner herein, qua filing of the instant petition.
It was further submitted that the petitioner herein, had filed the instant petition via a PoA. Hence, the petitioner does not have any right qua filing the instant petition/assailing the FIR.

7. At this juncture, the Officer present in Court had drawn the attention of this Court towards the contents of the factual report furnished by him, and had averred that the instant dispute pertains to making of forged documents, for instance, the will for the property and rent agreement.

Nevertheless, the statements made by the petitioner are contrary, as at one instance the petitioner has referred himself as the tenants qua the said property and on the other, have created false and fabricated documents, declaring themselves as the owner of the property in question.

8. Learned Public Prosecutor had further contended that the contention made by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the complainant had lodged two FIRs/complaints qua identical issues, is a misnomer.
Moreover, both the complaints are made to be registered by two different persons, though qua identical issue/subject matter.
Therefore, the same cannot constitute civil proceedings.
Lastly, learned counsel had submitted that qua the first FIR, the police authorities have already filed a Final Report.
9. Heard and considered.

10. Upon an assiduous scanning of the record, considering the aforementioned facts and circumstances of the case and taking note of the arguments averred by the learned counsel for both the parties, this Court deems it apposite to dismiss the instant petition for the reasons noted herein below:
10.1

That the contents of the factual report dated 02.09.2024 makes it unambiguous that the instant matter pertains to creation of forged and fabricated documents i.e.
rent agreement and will.
10.2 That this Court is satisfied with the contentions made by learned Public Prosecutor qua the fact that the instant FIRs/Complaints are made to be registered by two different persons.
10.3 That the matter in hand has certain dubious issue of facts, which can only be elucidated after conducting a free, unbiased investigation.

10.4 That the aspect about the complicity of a person who is involved in the forgery is a disputed question of fact and the same will have to be addressed after a proper appreciation of evidence which can be done only during trial and not at such a nascent stage when summons is served.

11. Therefore, in summation of the aforementioned facts and circumstances and the Factual Report dated 02.09.2024, this Court is of the view that the Hon'ble Apex Court in a catena of judgments has opined that while exercising inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973, the High Court is not supposed to hold a mini trial.

Therefore, while placing reliance upon the ratio encapsulated in CBI Vs. Aryan Singh [2024:RJ-JP:41460] (5 of 5) [CRLMP-5288/2024] reported in 2023 SCC OnLine SC 379; Dharambeer Kumar Singh Vs. State of Jharkhand (SLP Criminal Appeal No. 1500 of 2024), Supriya Jain v. State of Haryana reported in (2023) 7 SCC 711; Gulam Mustafa v. State of Karnataka, reported in 2023 SCC OnLine SC 603, this Court is of the opinion that as per the cardinal principle of law,
at the stage of discharge and/or quashing of the criminal proceedings, while exercising the powers under Section 482 Cr. P.C., the Court is not required to conduct the mini-trial.

At the stage of discharge and/or while exercising the powers under Section 482 Cr. P.C., the Court has very limited jurisdiction and is required to consider whether any sufficient material is available to proceed further against the accused for which the accused is required to be tried or not.
12.
In light of the aforementioned facts and circumstances, the instant petition being devoid of any merit stands dismissed.
No orders as to cost.
Pending applications, if any, shall also stand disposed of.
